title: Reusable barrier
hints: One closed channel wakes **every** goroutine waiting on it, which is exactly "release them all". Each round needs its own channel, because a closed channel can't be reopened.

`New` makes the first `release` channel. In `Wait`, under the mutex: remember the current `round` and `release`, then `count++`. If you are not the last, unlock and block on `<-release`. If you are the last (`count == n`), reset `count`, bump `round`, make a **new** `release` for the next round, unlock, and `close` the old one.

```go
b.mu.Lock()
round, release := b.round, b.release
b.count++
if b.count == b.n {
	b.count = 0
	b.round++
	b.release = make(chan struct{})
	b.mu.Unlock()
	close(release)
	return round
}
b.mu.Unlock()
<-release
return round
```
Copy `release` into a local **before** unlocking: by the time a waiter wakes up, `b.release` already belongs to the next round.
